formalization.project_name: Omega-bounded Sigma-products and a sharp compactness criterion

mathematical_sources.note: Directly consulted primary PDF, SHA256 7e040ba18193c87cb789c178cb74fbc3733bf4b3dc55a4eed719b8f6305d653f. Printed p.1 defines omega-boundedness; printed p.4 defines countable-support Sigma-products. Proposition 2.4 and its coordinate-closure proof on printed p.5 provide the omega-bounded specialization obtained by taking the dense core D equal to each whole factor. The full omega-bounded-pracompact dense-core theorem is not formalized. Example 2.5, printed pp.5–6, explains why the T1 premise cannot simply be omitted; that counterexample itself is not formalized. Printed pp.2 and 4 establish topological-algebra and productivity context. The sharp compact-Hausdorff compactness criterion and Boolean contrast are separately proved companions, not attributed as statements of Proposition 2.4. No novelty or original-priority claim.
mathematical_sources.title: On old and new classes of feebly compact spaces, arXiv:1804.07454v3

related_formalizations.note: Uses canonical product/subtype topology, Tychonoff compact-set products, closure/embedding lemmas and canonical countable compactness. These are upstream infrastructure, not new contributions.

Earlier campaign package proves Frechet-Urysohn convergence for first-countable factors and countable closure support for T1 factors, not omega-boundedness or the compactness criterion. The support definition and supporting finite-coordinate density argument are reused in standalone form with attribution. No earlier project package is imported.
